title: Cleanup job and DOT scope lookup depend on RT.access_token link
answers: why does refresh token access_token link matter
what determines refresh token expiry in oauth cleanup
how are scopes chosen on non-rotating refresh
body:
For non-rotating refresh tokens, OAuthRefreshToken.access_token must point at the most recent access token. Enforced in posthog/api/oauth/views.py `_save_bearer_token`.
Why: (1) the daily cleanup deletes an RT by the expiry of its linked AT; (2) django-oauth-toolkit reads next-refresh scopes from the linked AT; (3) upstream revoke deletes the linked AT, so revoking an RT now hits the latest AT, not the auth-code AT.
If skipped: in-use RTs get deleted, and scope narrowing/ceiling_scopes behave inconsistently. Tests such as test_dcr_refresh_token_revoke_from_other_client_does_not_sweep_session in posthog/api/oauth/test_views.py must watch the auth-code AT (unlinked) to verify no session sweep.
says: Refresh token expired before its linked access token
Why did changing refresh token scopes have inconsistent effects
Refresh token cleanup is removing tokens still actively in use
Access token expiry determines how long refresh tokens remain valid
Which access token defines the scope ceiling for refresh tokens

Failure to maintain this link causes in-use RTs to be deleted and scope narrowing/ceiling_scopes to behave inconsistently. Tests must watch the auth-code AT (unlinked, not just the linked one) to verify no unintended session sweep; see test_dcr_client_refresh_token_is_not_rotated. Applies to OAuth refresh, revoke, and scope logic in posthog/api/oauth/views.py.
